sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *cualquiera que*, *quienquiera que* and *dondequiera que* from B2 Unit 14. They say "whichever", "whoever" and "wherever", and they take the subjunctive because the answer is left open. Borders are a good place for them: whoever arrives, wherever they cross, whatever route they take.

items.spanish: Cualquier persona que llegue a la frontera necesita información clara.
items.english: Anyone who reaches the border needs clear information.

items.spanish: Quienquiera que cruce sin documentos corre más riesgos.
items.english: Whoever crosses without papers runs more risks.

items.spanish: Dondequiera que vayan los migrantes, necesitan documentos.
items.english: Wherever migrants go, they need documents.

items.spanish: Cualquiera que sea la ruta, el viaje es largo.
items.english: Whatever the route, the journey is long.

sections.content: Before a noun use *cualquier* (*cualquier persona que llegue*), never *cualquiera persona*. The subjunctive says "it does not matter which"; for a known person, use the indicative: *La persona que llegó pidió ayuda.*
